newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Zaire's Kamanda warns of partition.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's Kamanda warns of partition.

text.p: Zairean Foreign Minister Kamanda wa Kamanda warned on Monday that rebels controlling about a fifth of the central African country might be seeking its partition rather than full control.
He told Belgian radio during an informal visit to Brussels that efforts by the rebels to capture territory had "the seeds and the risks of a partition of Zaire."
The dividing line would run through the east of the country along "the 25th parallel which goes from Kisangani in Upper Zaire, to Kamina and Shaba (province)," he said.
The rebellion by the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire, led by Laurent Kabila, started near the eastern border with Rwanda and Burundi five months ago.

The Kinshasa government has now lost control over about a fifth of Zaire. It held an emergency cabinet meeting to discuss the fall two days ago of Kisangani, the biggest setback to ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko in the rebellion.
Kamanda accused the European Union and the United Nations of having abandoned Zaire and of having failed to put pressure on Kabila to observe a U.N. peace plan including a ceasefire.
"The (U.N.) Security Council should now draw the necessary conclusions" and force Kabila to accept a ceasefire, he said.

The rebels have said they will not agree to a ceasefire before negotiations and insist talks must centre on the departure from power of Mobutu, who has ruled Africa's third largest country for 32 years.
The ruler has spent much of his time at his luxury home in France since he underwent prostate cancer surgery last August.

The fighting in east Zaire has driven hundreds of thousands of Rwandan refugees into the wilderness. The U.N. refugee agency warned on Monday they faced death from starvation if aid workers were not given full access to them soon.
